```python
# Test cases for wrap_(text, width)

# 1. Basic wrapping (words fit perfectly or need breaking)
assert wrap_("Hello world", 5) == ["Hello", "world"], (wrap_("Hello world", 5), ["Hello", "world"])

# 2. Word longer than width (must be broken)
assert wrap_("Supercalifragilistic", 5) == ["Super", "calif", "ragil", "istic"], (wrap_("Supercalifragilistic", 5), ["Super", "calif", "ragil", "istic"])

# 3. Tabs are expanded (default tabsize 8)
# "\t" becomes 8 spaces. "a\tb" with width 10: "a" + 8 spaces + "b" = 10 chars.
assert wrap_("a\tb", 10) == ["a        b"], (wrap_("a\tb", 10), ["a        b"])

# 4. Tabs expanded and wrapped
# "\t" becomes 8 spaces. "a\tb" with width 5: "a" + 8 spaces exceeds 5.
# The spaces are treated as individual characters.
assert wrap_("a\tb", 5) == ["a", "     ", "b"], (wrap_("a\tb", 5), ["a", "     ", "b"])

# 5. Whitespace characters become one space (runs NOT collapsed)
# "a  b" (two spaces) with width 3: "a  " fits, "b" on next line.
assert wrap_("a  b", 3) == ["a  ", "b"], (wrap_("a  b", 3), ["a  ", "b"])

# 6. Whitespace at each line break is dropped (trailing/leading)
# "a b " with width 1: "a" fits, " b " has leading space dropped, "b" fits, trailing space dropped.
assert wrap_("a b ", 1) == ["a", "b"], (wrap_("a b ", 1), ["a", "b"])

# 7. Leading whitespace of the whole text is kept
# "  hello" with width 10: "  hello"
assert wrap_("  hello", 10) == ["  hello"], (wrap_("  hello", 10), ["  hello"])

# 8. Complex mix: leading ws, tabs, long words, and multiple spaces
# "  \ta  longword" width 5
# 1. Expand tab: "  " + "        " + "a  longword" -> "                  a  longword"
# 2. Leading ws: "                  " (10 spaces)
# 3. Content: "a  longword"
# 4. Wrap content at 5: "a  lo", "ngwor", "d"
# 5. Prepend leading ws to first line: "                  a  lo"
# Note: The logic in the provided function handles the leading whitespace by prepending it to the first result line.
# Let's verify a simpler version of this to ensure the logic holds:
assert wrap_("  a b", 1) == ["  ", "a", "b"], (wrap_("  a b", 1), ["  ", "a", "b"])

# 9. Empty string or only whitespace
assert wrap_("", 10) == [], (wrap_("", 10), [])
assert wrap_("   ", 10) == [], (wrap_("   ", 10), [])

# 10. Word exactly matching width
assert wrap_("abcde", 5) == ["abcde"], (wrap_("abcde", 5), ["abcde"])

# 11. Multiple spaces between words
# "a    b" width 3: "a  " fits, "  b" -> leading space dropped -> "b"
assert wrap_("a    b", 3) == ["a  ", "b"], (wrap_("a    b", 3), ["a  ", "b"])
```
